flashcard_questions.q: What is regeneration in an urban area?
flashcard_questions.a: Reversing the decline of an area by improving its buildings and infrastructure.
Land previously built on or used for industry that is available for redevelopment.

flashcard_questions.q: What stood on the Liverpool ONE site before the shopping complex was built?
flashcard_questions.a: A bus station surrounded by derelict buildings.

flashcard_questions.q: Liverpool ONE provides ____ underground car parking spaces.
The regeneration of Anfield is a partnership project worth ____.
How many new homes have been built in Anfield since 2013?
What did the 2024 Taylor Swift concerts generate for the economy around Anfield?
What is an integrated transport system?
flashcard_questions.a: A network where different forms of transport link together so passengers can switch easily.

flashcard_questions.q: Which pre-paid travel card covers Liverpool's buses, trains, ferries and e-scooters?
flashcard_questions.a: The Metro Card, formerly called the Walrus Card.
The spreading of a city outwards into the surrounding countryside.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does urban sprawl on the rural-urban fringe increase flood risk?
flashcard_questions.a: New buildings and roads create impermeable surfaces, so rainwater cannot soak into the ground.

flashcard_questions.q: What effect does the growth of commuter settlements have on local house prices?
flashcard_questions.a: Prices rise, so local residents on low incomes are priced out.

flashcard_questions.q: What year is Liverpool City Council's net zero target?
Liverpool City Council has cut ____ tonnes of CO₂ since 2005.
What percentage of Liverpool's emissions comes from homes?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term-to-definition (regeneration, brownfield, integrated transport, urban sprawl), 5 case-study-to-fact with one figure each (Anfield homes, Taylor Swift income, net zero year, emissions share, Liverpool ONE parking), 3 cloze on statistics, 2 cause-to-consequence (sprawl and flood risk, commuters and house prices), 1 strategy-to-example (Metro Card). Dropped the £1 house scheme count and the three-bin recycling detail to keep numeric cards from interfering.
